question.text: Under the Reverse Mortgage Loan Enabled Annuity (RMLEA) Scheme, what is the starting loan-to-value (LTV) ratio for borrowers in the age group 60-70 years?

explanation.text: The Logic: Under RMLEA, the loan-to-value ratio starts at 60% of the property value for borrowers aged 60-70 years and increases for higher age brackets, going up to 75% for those aged 80 and above. The 60% starting LTV provides a buffer for the lending institution against property value fluctuations over the loan tenure. The Trap: 80% and 90% are common LTV ratios for regular home loans but the reverse mortgage starting LTV is lower due to the uncertainty of loan tenure and long-horizon property-value risk. Note: NISM Series XVII (pages 187-189) sets the RMLEA starting LTV at 60% for age 60-70 and the maximum at 75% for age 80 and above.
